# Model card: frozen Phikon + linear head (demo model)

Format inspired by Mitchell et al., *Model Cards for Model Reporting* (2019). This card describes the model of
the demo app ([app/](app/)); the other methods of the project are compared in the [README](README.md).

## Model details

- **Architecture:** Phikon ViT-B/16 (Owkin, pretrained on histology), frozen, pinned revision; its [CLS] token
  is standardized with the mean and standard deviation of the training patches, then a linear layer gives a
  tumor score.
- **Training:** the linear layer only, with the WILDS ERM protocol (SGD, 10 epochs), on the training hospitals
  of Camelyon17-WILDS. Seed 0, chosen on the validation hospital (see Selection).
- **Post-processing:** temperature 0.87, fitted on the validation hospital; patches whose score
  is not confident enough are referred to a pathologist (cutoff chosen on the validation hospital).
- **Explanation:** heat map by Grad-CAM at the input of the last transformer block (14 x 14 grid).
- **Licenses:** code MIT; Phikon weights under the Owkin non-commercial license, so the model is for
  non-commercial research and education only.

## Intended use

- Demonstrating, for research and teaching, how a metastasis detector behaves on a hospital it was not
  trained on: score, heat map, referral of uncertain patches.
- **Not a medical device. Not for diagnosis or any clinical decision.**

## Out of scope

Whole-slide or patient-level diagnosis; other organs, stains or magnifications than 96 x 96 H&E lymph-node
patches of Camelyon17-WILDS (other images are cropped and resized, and the output is unreliable); commercial use.

## Data

- **Training:** Camelyon17-WILDS train split, hospitals 0, 3 and 4 (302,436 patches).
- **Selection:** validation hospital (hospital 1, 34,904 patches, 8 patients), never seen
  in training.
- **Test:** hospital 2 (85,054 patches, 9 patients), never seen in training and never
  used to choose anything.
- No demographic information is available, so performance across patient groups could not be assessed.

## Selection

The method was chosen as the best one on the validation hospital (mean of 4 seeds), and the seed as
the one with the highest validation accuracy (seed 0: 97.12%, seed 1: 97.00%, seed 2: 97.10%, seed 3: 97.11%): the seeds are equivalent, the rule just
picks one without looking at the test hospital.

## Results of this model

| Patches | Accuracy | AUC |
|---|---|---|
| Training hospitals (id_val, held-out patches of the training slides) | 99.0% | 0.999 |
| Validation hospital (used for selection) | 97.1% | 0.995 |
| Test hospital (unseen, never used to choose) | **93.2%** | 0.985 |

- Over 4 seeds, the method reaches 93.9% on the test hospital, 95% interval
  [84.0, 98.0] when its patients are redrawn: with 9 patients, the uncertainty
  is large.
- **Referral:** on the validation hospital, the model answers 80% of patches by design. On the
  test hospital it answers 68%, and its error drops from 6.8% to
  1.0% on the answered patches.
- **Calibration:** expected calibration error on the test hospital 0.044 before and
  0.046 after the temperature fitted on the validation hospital. The score is calibrated for
  one hospital only; elsewhere it is a ranking, not an exact probability.

## Checks

- The demo reproduces the saved predictions of this run (largest probability gap 0.0016,
  100% of decisions identical on 200 validation patches) ([results/tables/app_checks.json](results/tables/app_checks.json)).
- The heat map depends on the learned weights: with the last block randomized, its rank correlation with the
  original map falls to 0.07.

## Caveats

- Two unseen hospitals only; nothing guarantees the results on a third one.
- Labels come from hand-drawn contours and describe the central 32 x 32 region of each patch; some patches
  that every method gets wrong are candidates for ambiguous labels.
- A heat map shows where the score's gradient is strong, not the model's reasoning.
